rationale: The notation is reader-facing and native-size display avoids preventable resampling blur.

source_location: record 196, Fisher citation and publisher statement

target_correction: The target gives Annals of Eugenics 7, 355–369 and renders the statement coherently in Indonesian.
rationale: The DOI record and article pagination establish 355–369; the duplicated words do not alter the warning's intended meaning.

source_text: The one-dimensional scaling introduces an unused y=Y sqrt(r/D).
target_correction: The target removes the extraneous y scaling and retains n, x, and tau.
rationale: The model and transformed PDE are explicitly one-dimensional.

source_text: After defining dimensionless time tau, the substitution and time derivative revert to t without declaring a rename.
target_correction: The target consistently uses n(x,tau), xi=x-c tau, and partial n/partial tau.
rationale: The preceding nondimensionalization and Equation 9.8 use tau.

source_text: Local saddle and node-or-spiral classifications are presented as proof of a global connecting trajectory for every positive c.
target_correction: The target states that local classification alone is insufficient and makes the physical front depend on the global unstable-manifold branch.
rationale: A heteroclinic connection is a global property not implied by the eigenvalue types alone.

source_location: record 196, Fisher-KPP admissible and selected speeds
source_text: The text excludes the critical speed c=2 and says one front is selected without an initial-data hypothesis.
target_correction: The target includes the degenerate critical front at c=2 and states the steep/compact-support versus shallow-tail selection qualification.
rationale: The Fisher-KPP threshold is c at least 2; asymptotic speed selection depends on the leading-edge decay of the initial data.

source_text: A span begins outside footnote 3 and closes inside it, producing crossed markup and an orphaned span in rendered HTML.
target_correction: The target closes each styled span within the footnote boundary before resuming the surrounding sentence.
rationale: Balanced nesting is required for deterministic accessible HTML conversion.

source_text: The printed chemotactic term chi grad(n) permits nonzero bacterial flux where bacterial density b is zero.
target_correction: The target uses chi b grad(n)-D grad(b).
rationale: The density-weighted Keller-Segel flux vanishes with b and is dimensionally consistent with bacterial transport.

source_text: The prompt omits a step length and does not distinguish mean signed displacement from typical spread.
target_correction: The target declares unit steps and separately asks for N(2p-1) and the fluctuation scale about that mean.
rationale: Without those distinctions, 'how far' is ambiguous between expectation, absolute distance, and standard deviation.

source_text: The source contains 'n point outwards', 'me make', 'regions regions', 'of equivalently', 'particle are', 'particles star', 'are are', and 'diffusion describe'.
target_correction: The target supplies grammatically correct Indonesian at all eight locations.
rationale: These are unambiguous agreement, duplication, or word-choice errors and do not change mathematical content.

source_text: The chapter refers to an unavailable MATLAB diffusion GUI and two PPLANE plots but freezes no executable code, seed, initial conditions, or numerical settings.
target_correction: The edition adds one independently authored deterministic NumPy/SciPy/Matplotlib companion for the random walk and Fisher-KPP phase-plane investigations.
rationale: The open companion restores reproducible computation without importing or imitating proprietary source code.

source_text: The phrase 'with which this author agrees' follows a Fisher citation and can be misread as attributing the modern publisher statement to Fisher.
target_correction: The target explicitly identifies the agreeing party as the author of this chapter.
rationale: The statement is modern publisher context reproduced by the living chapter author, not language attributable to Fisher.

source_text: The DOI anchor covers only the word 'The' in the cited article title.
target_correction: The target places the complete article title inside the unchanged DOI anchor.
rationale: Descriptive link text makes the citation destination intelligible to screen-reader and keyboard users.

source_text: The real-part operator is printed as Re e(lambda_k).
target_correction: The target uses operatorname{Re}(lambda_k).
rationale: The extra e is a definite transcription error and the displayed equality requires the real part.

source_text: The dependent variable is written psi(x,t) although every ansatz also contains p y.
target_correction: The three target ansatzes use psi(x,y,t).
rationale: The equation and exponential are explicitly two-dimensional.

source_text: Problems 1 and 2 omit existence conditions and Problem 3 asks for omega q and p but not the displayed growth exponent lambda.
target_correction: The target asks for the existence conditions in Problems 1 and 2 and includes lambda among the outputs in Problem 3.
rationale: For allowed parameter values some purely oscillatory modes do not exist; the general ansatz is not solved unless lambda is determined.

source_text: The prose caption ends Omega greater than 0 with an unmatched dollar sign.
target_correction: The target removes the stray dollar sign.
rationale: It is an unambiguous markup typo outside a TeX shortcode.

source_text: The prose says the model parameters may be real or complex although the next sentence declares all parameters real.
target_correction: The target states that the coefficients may be real or complex.
rationale: The imaginary-part parameters determine whether the resulting coefficients are real or complex.

source_text: A time-independent Fourier mode is said to have time derivative lambda_k u_k.
target_correction: The target states that the spatial Fourier mode is an eigenfunction of the linear operator with eigenvalue lambda_k.
rationale: A time derivative requires a time-dependent amplitude; the eigenfunction statement yields the same dispersion relation without that missing dependence.

source_text: The source reads 'Defect of the hexagonal pattern take'.
target_correction: The target supplies grammatical plural agreement in Indonesian.
rationale: This is an unambiguous number-agreement error.

source_text: The footnote hard-codes 'Footnote #7' without a semantic target.
target_correction: The target refers to the two review articles cited above.
rationale: The semantic reference remains correct if footnotes are renumbered and is intelligible without a fragile counter.

source_text: The DOI anchor covers only 'Swift-Hohenberg' inside the longer article title.
target_correction: The target places the complete article title inside the unchanged DOI anchor.
rationale: Descriptive link text exposes the destination to assistive technology.

source_text: All three figures are displayed above intrinsic resolution and Figure 10.1 is a mixed-photo collage without component-level credit in the record.
target_correction: The reader displays Figures 10.2 and 10.3 at intrinsic size and replaces Figure 10.1 with a separately provenanced independent accessible SVG while retaining the exact source witness.
rationale: This avoids blur and an unresolved component-rights dependency without copying source pixels.

source_text: The proprietary GUI is named but no URL code binary data parameters grid timestep or seed is supplied.
target_correction: The edition adds one independently authored deterministic NumPy/SciPy/Matplotlib companion for growth rates spectral pattern formation and Klausmeier checks.
rationale: The open companion restores reproducible computation without importing or imitating unavailable MATLAB code.

source_text: The source calls an unspecified set a vector space if and only if it is closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
target_correction: The target states the valid subspace criterion for a nonempty subset of an ambient real or complex vector space.
rationale: Closure alone does not supply the field operations and axioms for an arbitrary set; nonemptiness plus inherited operations is required for the subspace test.

source_text: The set is written with plain S and the coefficient quantifier is malformed as a subset relation.
target_correction: The target uses mathematical S consistently and quantifies alpha_1 through alpha_n over the relevant scalar field.
rationale: The revised notation states the definition of linear independence unambiguously without changing its content.

source_text: The TeX contains resp. or where and English ordinal suffixes inside Indonesian mathematical prose.
target_correction: The target localizes formula text to atau and dengan and removes the redundant th suffixes after Indonesian ke-.
rationale: Reader-facing mathematical text should be natural Indonesian while symbols and meaning remain unchanged.

source_text: The source says every n-dimensional vector space is isomorphic to real n-space without specifying the scalar field.
target_correction: The target restricts the statement to real vector spaces.
rationale: An n-dimensional complex vector space is isomorphic to complex n-space rather than real n-space as a vector space over the stated field.

source_text: The source writes (A^T_ij)=(A_ji), which ambiguously puts the indices inside the superscripted matrix symbol and wraps scalar entries as matrices.
target_correction: The target writes (A^T)_ij=A_ji.
rationale: The corrected notation states the entrywise definition of transpose.

source_text: The source says i is one row of A.
target_correction: The target says i is a fixed row index of A.
rationale: Laplace expansion fixes an index and sums over the complementary index; i is an index, not a row object.

source_text: The equivalence list says AX=b has exactly one solution without quantifying b and changes the unknown from lowercase x used immediately above.
target_correction: The target states that Ax=b has exactly one solution for every right-hand side.
rationale: Unique solvability for one particular b is not equivalent to invertibility; the assertion requires every b.

source_text: A is declared real while eigenvalues may be nonreal but the scalar extension for the eigenvectors is left unstated.
target_correction: The target explicitly says the vector space is complexified when a nonreal eigenvalue is considered.
rationale: A real matrix can have nonreal eigenpairs only after extending scalars to the complex numbers.

source_text: The source requires m not equal to 1 and only (A-aI)f nonzero, which excludes ordinary eigenvectors and does not define the exact rank of a Jordan chain.
target_correction: The target permits positive m and requires (A-aI)^(m-1)f nonzero together with (A-aI)^m f=0.
rationale: This is the standard exact-rank definition and includes ordinary eigenvectors as rank-one generalized eigenvectors.

source_text: Equation (A1.2) uses I after the preceding sentence defines I_n.
target_correction: The target uses I_n in (A1.2).
rationale: The subscript preserves the declared matrix dimension and removes a harmless but definite notation inconsistency.

source_text: The source states the root count trace sum and determinant product without saying repeated eigenvalues are counted with algebraic multiplicity.
target_correction: The target adds the algebraic-multiplicity qualification to all three statements.
rationale: Without multiplicity the three standard identities are incomplete for repeated eigenvalues.

source_text: The source says eigenvectors form a subspace and every vector space is the sum of ordinary eigenspaces.
target_correction: The target distinguishes the eigenspace including zero from its nonzero eigenvectors and restricts direct-sum decomposition into ordinary eigenspaces to diagonalizable matrices while noting the general alternatives.
rationale: Eigenvectors alone omit zero and are not a subspace; a defective matrix does not have a basis of ordinary eigenvectors.

source_text: Each four-entry column vector is declared with an array of four columns.
target_correction: The target declares all five vectors with one-column arrays.
rationale: The source environment specification conflicts with the displayed column-vector entries and can produce excess spacing or malformed rendering.

source_text: The source states a unique fastest-increase direction and normal-to-level-surface property without excluding critical points.
target_correction: The target restricts those direction and regular-level-surface statements to points where the gradient is nonzero and identifies the maximum over unit directions.
rationale: At a critical point the gradient has no direction and the corresponding level set need not be a regular surface.

source_text: The source calls the one-equation constraint in three variables a curve and omits the regularity and local-necessity qualifications.
target_correction: The target states the necessary parallel-gradient condition for a local extremum at a regular point of the constraint surface.
rationale: A regular set g(x,y,z)=C is generally a surface and the multiplier condition requires a nonzero constraint gradient.

source_text: The source squares the vector derivative dr/dt without a norm and introduces v without identifying it as speed.
target_correction: The target uses the squared Euclidean norm of dr/dt and identifies v as the speed.
rationale: Kinetic energy is one half m times speed squared; a bare vector square is undefined in this context.

source_text: The source writes V(r) but subsequently evaluates V at the vector r without defining scalar r as a radial coordinate.
target_correction: The target writes V(vector r) consistently.
rationale: The force is the gradient of a potential on position space; the unannounced scalar argument is inconsistent.

source_text: The source invokes a domain with no codimension-one holes as the sufficient topological hypothesis.
target_correction: The target uses the standard sufficient condition of an open simply connected domain.
rationale: The source wording is nonstandard and can miss loop obstructions to a global potential.

source_text: The source names the graph z=f(x,y) but evaluates F at an undefined z(x,y) and does not state the orientation represented by the displayed normal.
target_correction: The target evaluates F at (x,y,f(x,y)) and states that the formula uses the upward orientation.
rationale: The displayed vector (-f_x,-f_y,1) is the upward-oriented area vector for the named graph.

source_text: The source writes the undefined limit W to 0 and divides by a prose volume expression.
target_correction: The target gives the flux-per-volume limit over shrinking balls centered at P.
rationale: A local limit needs an explicit family of regions shrinking to the evaluation point.

source_text: The source says the domain is closed and has no holes as a sufficient hypothesis for a vector potential.
target_correction: The target states the sound sufficient condition of an open star-shaped domain.
rationale: Closed is not the relevant domain property and no holes is not a precise cohomological condition; star-shaped is a clear sufficient hypothesis.

source_location: record 413, curl direction and maximum circulation density
source_text: The source assigns a direction to curl at every point and refers to that direction when describing its magnitude.
target_correction: The target restricts the directional statement to nonzero curl and identifies its magnitude as the maximum circulation density over unit directions.
rationale: The zero vector has no direction; the norm is the maximum projection over unit vectors.

source_text: The source specifies a simple closed curve but omits a boundary-regularity hypothesis.
target_correction: The target requires the simple closed curve to be piecewise smooth while preserving the positive-orientation and domain hypotheses.
rationale: The standard line-integral form of Green's theorem requires a sufficiently regular boundary such as a piecewise-smooth simple closed curve.
